# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 72/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 72. High = (16.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 72.

This is a small Next.js App Router site. I read every file in it and sampled five routes: `/`, `/pricing`, `/docs`, `/blog` and `/thank-you`. The basics are mostly sound. The gaps are no `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt, no `lang` on `<html>`, a noindexed pricing page that the sitemap and menu both list, and a blog that loads its posts only in the browser. Every result was read from code, and nothing came from a live site.

## Live check

**Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Point robots.txt at your sitemap
- **Why it matters:** crawlers read robots.txt first, and right now it doesn't tell them your sitemap exists.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:6`
- **What the code says:** the file ends at `Disallow: /` (the GPTBot group) and has no `Sitemap:` line. The sitemap is at `public/sitemap.xml`.
- **Size:** Small. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`.
- **Score after this:** 80 (GEO-011 goes from 0 to 2 of 2 points).

### 2. Set the page language and give the blog its own title and description
- **Why it matters:** `lang` tells machines which language the site is in. The blog currently shows the same default title and description as the home page.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11` and `app/blog/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `<html>` has no `lang`. `blog/page.tsx` is `'use client'`, so it can't export `metadata`, and it falls back to the layout default.
- **Size:** Small. Use `<html lang="en">`, and add an `app/blog/layout.tsx` that exports `metadata`.
- **Score after this:** 80 (GEO-012 goes from 0 to 2 of 2 points).

### 3. Add a canonical link to /docs and /blog
- **Why it matters:** a canonical link tells search engines which address is the main one for a page, so they don't have to guess between duplicates.
- **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1` and `app/blog/page.tsx`
- **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };` has no `alternates.canonical`. `/blog` has none either.
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 76 (GEO-015 goes from 1 to 2 of 2 points).

Doing all three gives about 85 (19.5 ÷ 23). That also needs a canonical on `/blog`, and the blog metadata from item 2.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is valid. |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` allows `*`. Only GPTBot (a training crawler) is blocked, which matches `trainingCrawlers: block`. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` has `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`, and `/pricing` is in the sitemap and the nav. 3 of 4 routes are clear, so 2.25 of 3 points. |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your own domain | Problem | Not run | `/` and `/pricing` are clear. `/docs` and `/blog` have none. 2 of 4 routes are clear, so 1 of 2 points. |
| GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `app/blog/page.tsx:8` has `fetch('/api/posts')` inside `useEffect`. The other 3 routes are server-rendered, so 2.25 of 3 points. |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found. |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid, but `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line. 0 of 2 points. |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Problem | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:11` has `<html>` with no `lang`, so every route fails. `/blog` also shows the layout default title and description. 0 of 2 points. |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are linked with plain links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:13` has plain `<a href>` links to all four pages. |
| GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Clear | Not run | Only `data-nosnippet` on one element at `app/layout.tsx:15`, which is fine. No middleware and no `next.config`. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | I read the layout and all five pages. There are no images, and the links have text. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared. |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. This is optional and not scored. |

## Other problems found

- `/pricing` carries a canonical and sits in the sitemap while it is `noindex`. This sends mixed signals. Remove `robots: { index: false ... }` at `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`, or drop it from the sitemap at `public/sitemap.xml:4` and from the nav.
- `app/blog/page.tsx:8` fetches `/api/posts`, and no `app/api` route exists in the repo. If the endpoint lives elsewhere, ignore this. Otherwise the blog will always render empty.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live status codes and headers:** whether pages answer 200, and any `X-Robots-Tag` header set outside the repo. A live scan with your URL would show these.
- **Blog content:** a live check would show how much text the server sends for `/blog`.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site, which matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: allow`.
- `/thank-you` is intentionally noindexed. It isn't in the sitemap or the nav, so I didn't count it.
- `https://www.ledger.example` is the site's own domain, from `geo.config.json`.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
